title: Precalculus: Functions, Models, and Change
subtitle: Functions, Models, and Change
description: A continuous Precalculus course built around functions, multiple representations, exact reasoning, modeling, and change.

units.title: Algebra and Function Readiness
units.description: A readiness diagnostic separates prerequisite strands so that a learner receives targeted repair rather than one vague total score.
outcomes: Use diagnostic evidence to identify which prerequisite strands are secure and which require targeted repair.
Classify and solve common equation and inequality families while distinguishing reversible steps from candidate-generating steps.
Recognize and apply the principal factoring structures needed for polynomial-function analysis.
Simplify and solve rational expressions while preserving every restriction from the original form.
Move among radical and rational-exponent forms, simplify exact values, and reject extraneous candidates.
Apply exponent and logarithm laws, convert between inverse forms, and solve basic equations with valid domains.
Evaluate functions, solve output conditions, and read domain, range, intercepts, extrema, and intervals from graphs.
Select methods across prerequisite strands, justify restrictions, and communicate exact and approximate results.

units.title: Functions and Multiple Representations
units.description: An input is supplied to a relationship, an output is determined by it, and parameters remain fixed for one selected model.
outcomes: Identify the input, output, parameters, and units in a quantitative relationship and explain how the quantities depend on one another.
Determine whether a relation is a function by applying the rule that each allowed input has exactly one output.
Use function notation accurately and distinguish finding an output from finding inputs that produce a chosen output.
Translate a function relationship among verbal, tabular, graphical, and algebraic representations while preserving quantities, units, and domain.
Determine the real domain of a function by combining denominator, even-root, logarithm, and composition restrictions.
Distinguish the algebraic domain of a formula from the inputs that are meaningful in a model.
Read range, intercepts, extrema, boundedness, symmetry, and intervals of increase or decrease from a graph.
Evaluate, graph, and interpret functions that use different rules on different parts of the domain.
Calculate and interpret average rate of change as output change per input change and as the slope of a secant line.
Construct, compare, and defend function representations while stating assumptions, domain, units, and limitations.

units.title: Composition, Inverses, and Modeling
units.description: Composition represents an ordered chain in which the inner function acts first.

Build a multi-stage function model, state its domain and assumptions, and evaluate whether an inverse interpretation is meaningful.

lessons.title: Readiness diagnostic and routing
lessons.outcome: Use diagnostic evidence to identify which prerequisite strands are secure and which require targeted repair.
opening: A readiness diagnostic separates prerequisite strands so that a learner receives targeted repair rather than one vague total score.
This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use readiness diagnostic and routing to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.
prerequisites: Show algebraic steps in a checkable order.
exposition: Attempt each strand independently, compare reasoning as well as answers, route missed skills to a focused repair page, and use a different return check to confirm transfer.
The diagnostic is a routing tool, not a grade. A secure strand may be passed while another remains active for repair.
A symbolic answer is not complete by itself. In this lesson, the same claim must also be readable through readiness strand map, evidence-to-repair flow, or another equivalent representation.

guide.application: These algebra choices are the load-bearing steps beneath later work with functions. A restriction lost here can turn into a false intercept, a missing asymptote, or an invalid model several lessons later.
bigIdea: Precalculus is unforgiving about hidden algebra errors. The useful habit is to separate reversible algebra from steps that can create candidates, and to keep domain restrictions beside the work instead of trying to remember them at the end.

This lesson narrows that lens to one goal: use diagnostic evidence to identify which prerequisite strands are secure and which require targeted repair. lessons.title: Equation and inequality repair

lessons.title: Function representation and modeling studio
lessons.outcome: Construct, compare, and defend function representations while stating assumptions, domain, units, and limitations.
opening: A model is a deliberately simplified function used to answer a question; it is not the real system itself.
This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use function representation and modeling studio to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.
prerequisites: Use function notation from the algebra and function readiness unit.
Read ordered pairs and interval notation.
exposition: Define quantities, choose a family, estimate parameters, state domain and assumptions, inspect residuals, and revise or reject when evidence disagrees.
Interpolation and extrapolation must be distinguished, and causation requires evidence beyond correlation.
A symbolic answer is not complete by itself. In this lesson, the same claim must also be readable through modeling cycle, competing extrapolations, or another equivalent representation.

guide.application: The same dependency may arrive as a story, table, graph, or formula. Learning to preserve the inputs, outputs, units, and domain while moving among those forms is the central language of the course.
bigIdea: A function is a dependency, not merely an equation. Inputs, outputs, units, and domain must agree in words, tables, graphs, and formulas; each representation should tell the same mathematical story.

This lesson narrows that lens to one goal: construct, compare, and defend function representations while stating assumptions, domain, units, and limitations. The point is not to memorize an isolated trick; it is to know what evidence makes the conclusion valid and how a second representation can check it.
questions: What is the input and what is the output?
Which inputs are allowed?
Where is the same feature visible in another representation?
guide.verification: Choose two representations and make them verify one another. A table can test a formula, a graph can expose a domain or range claim, and units can reveal a model that is algebraically neat but conceptually wrong.

lessons.title: Coordinate mappings and transformation logic
lessons.outcome: Derive graph transformations by tracking how input-output pairs move.
opening: A graph transformation is a coordinate map from a point (u,v) on the parent to a point on the transformed graph.

This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use coordinate mappings and transformation logic to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.
prerequisites: Read domain, range, and key points.
exposition: Outside operations alter v; inside operations determine the new x by solving the inside expression equal to u.
For a f(b(x-h))+k, the map is (u,v) to (h+u/b,av+k).
A symbolic answer is not complete by itself. In this lesson, the same claim must also be readable through input-output machine, coordinate mapping table, or another equivalent representation.

This lesson narrows that lens to one goal: derive graph transformations by tracking how input-output pairs move. The point is not to memorize an isolated trick; it is to know what evidence makes the conclusion valid and how a second representation can check it.

routes.title: Precalculus: Functions, Models, and Change
routes.description: A continuous Precalculus course built around functions, multiple representations, exact reasoning, modeling, and change.

routes.title: Algebra and Function Readiness
routes.description: A readiness diagnostic separates prerequisite strands so that a learner receives targeted repair rather than one vague total score.

routes.title: Functions and Multiple Representations
routes.description: An input is supplied to a relationship, an output is determined by it, and parameters remain fixed for one selected model.

routes.title: Transformations and Function Operations
routes.description: A parent function is a convenient reference member identified by domain, range, symmetry, endpoints, asymptotes, and rate patterns.

routes.title: Composition, Inverses, and Modeling
routes.description: Composition represents an ordered chain in which the inner function acts first.

routes.title: Polynomial Functions
routes.description: Power functions f(x)=ax^p connect positive, negative, and fractional exponent behavior.

routes.title: Rational Functions
routes.description: A rational function P/Q excludes every real input where the original denominator Q is zero.

routes.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
routes.description: Constant first differences indicate additive linear change; constant ratios indicate multiplicative exponential change.

routes.title: Systems, Matrices, and Multivariable Models
routes.description: A system solution satisfies every equation simultaneously and appears graphically as a common intersection.

routes.title: Readiness diagnostic and routing
routes.description: Use diagnostic evidence to identify which prerequisite strands are secure and which require targeted repair.

routes.title: Equation and inequality repair
routes.description: Classify and solve common equation and inequality families while distinguishing reversible steps from candidate-generating steps.

routes.title: Factoring and polynomial structure repair
routes.description: Recognize and apply the principal factoring structures needed for polynomial-function analysis.

routes.title: Rational expressions and restrictions repair
routes.description: Simplify and solve rational expressions while preserving every restriction from the original form.

routes.title: Radicals and rational exponents repair
routes.description: Move among radical and rational-exponent forms, simplify exact values, and reject extraneous candidates.

routes.title: Exponential and logarithmic algebra repair
routes.description: Apply exponent and logarithm laws, convert between inverse forms, and solve basic equations with valid domains.

routes.title: Function notation and graph reading repair
routes.description: Evaluate functions, solve output conditions, and read domain, range, intercepts, extrema, and intervals from graphs.

routes.title: Mixed readiness synthesis
routes.description: Select methods across prerequisite strands, justify restrictions, and communicate exact and approximate results.

routes.title: Quantities, variables, and dependency
routes.description: Identify the input, output, parameters, and units in a quantitative relationship and explain how the quantities depend on one another.

routes.title: Relations and functions
routes.description: Determine whether a relation is a function by applying the rule that each allowed input has exactly one output.

routes.title: Function notation, evaluation, and solving
routes.description: Use function notation accurately and distinguish finding an output from finding inputs that produce a chosen output.

routes.title: Words, tables, graphs, and formulas
routes.description: Translate a function relationship among verbal, tabular, graphical, and algebraic representations while preserving quantities, units, and domain.

routes.title: Domain from formulas
routes.description: Determine the real domain of a function by combining denominator, even-root, logarithm, and composition restrictions.

routes.title: Domain from context
routes.description: Distinguish the algebraic domain of a formula from the inputs that are meaningful in a model.

routes.title: Range and global graph behavior
routes.description: Read range, intercepts, extrema, boundedness, symmetry, and intervals of increase or decrease from a graph.

routes.title: Piecewise-defined functions
routes.description: Evaluate, graph, and interpret functions that use different rules on different parts of the domain.

routes.title: Average rate of change
routes.description: Calculate and interpret average rate of change as output change per input change and as the slope of a secant line.

routes.title: Function representation and modeling studio
routes.description: Construct, compare, and defend function representations while stating assumptions, domain, units, and limitations.

routes.title: Parent-function atlas
routes.description: Recognize benchmark function families by domain, range, symmetry, intercepts, end behavior, and rate patterns.

routes.title: Coordinate mappings and transformation logic
routes.description: Derive graph transformations by tracking how input-output pairs move.

routes.title: Vertical translations
routes.description: Analyze how adding a constant outside a function changes outputs, range, intercepts, extrema, and asymptotes.

routes.title: Horizontal translations
routes.description: Analyze how replacing x by x-h changes input locations, domain, intercepts, extrema, and vertical asymptotes.

routes.title: Reflections and symmetry
routes.description: Reflect function graphs across coordinate axes and connect reflection rules with even and odd symmetry.

routes.title: Vertical and horizontal scaling
routes.description: Distinguish output scaling from input scaling and determine the resulting stretches, compressions, domains, and ranges.

routes.title: Combined transformations
routes.description: Analyze and graph functions with several transformations by tracking inputs, outputs, and key features.

routes.title: Sums and differences of functions
routes.description: Add and subtract functions pointwise, determine the common domain, and interpret combined outputs.

routes.title: Products and quotients of functions
routes.description: Multiply and divide functions pointwise while analyzing zeros, restrictions, and combined graph behavior.

routes.title: Reconstructing formulas from transformed graphs
routes.description: Use parent-family features, transformations, and one or more data points to construct and verify a function formula.

routes.title: Composition as sequential processing
routes.description: Interpret f composed with g as applying g first and then f, and explain why order generally matters.

routes.title: Composition from formulas
routes.description: Evaluate and simplify composite functions symbolically while preserving grouping and domain conditions.

routes.title: Composition from tables and graphs
routes.description: Evaluate composite functions when one or both functions are represented numerically or graphically.

routes.title: Domains of composite functions
routes.description: Determine the domain of a composite by enforcing both inner-function and outer-input conditions.

routes.title: One-to-one functions
routes.description: Determine whether a function is one-to-one and explain why one-to-one behavior is required for an inverse function.

routes.title: Constructing inverse functions
routes.description: Construct an inverse function algebraically and state the swapped domain and range.

routes.title: Graphs and verification of inverses
routes.description: Verify inverse functions using composition and graph symmetry across y=x.

routes.title: Domain restrictions and radical inverses
routes.description: Restrict power functions to one-to-one branches and connect those branches to principal radical functions.

routes.title: Model construction and validation
routes.description: Build a multi-stage function model, state its domain and assumptions, and evaluate whether an inverse interpretation is meaningful.

routes.title: Power functions and dominant behavior
routes.description: Compare power functions f(x)=ax^p and explain how exponent and coefficient control domain, symmetry, end behavior, and growth.

routes.title: Polynomial functions, degree, and leading term
routes.description: Identify degree, leading term, coefficients, and standard form, and explain why the leading term governs large-input behavior.

routes.title: End behavior
routes.description: Determine polynomial end behavior from degree parity and leading coefficient and express it verbally, graphically, and with limit-style notation.

routes.title: Zeros, factors, and intercepts
routes.description: Connect polynomial zeros, linear factors, solutions, and x-intercepts, and distinguish exact from approximate zeros.

routes.title: Multiplicity and sign behavior
routes.description: Relate the multiplicity of a zero to sign changes, crossing or touching behavior, and local flattening.

routes.title: Graph construction from structure
routes.description: Construct a polynomial graph from degree, leading coefficient, zeros, multiplicities, sign intervals, and selected points.

routes.title: Turning points and local versus global behavior
routes.description: Use degree bounds, graph evidence, and function values to analyze turning points and extrema.

routes.title: Intermediate Value reasoning and root bounds
routes.description: Use polynomial continuity and sign changes to guarantee roots and bracket them within intervals.

routes.title: Polynomial division
routes.description: Divide polynomials using long and synthetic division and verify the division algorithm P=DQ+R.

routes.title: Remainder and factor theorems
routes.description: Use P(c) as the remainder on division by x-c and test whether x-c is a factor.

routes.title: Rational-root candidates and root search
routes.description: Generate all possible rational zeros of an integer-coefficient polynomial and organize an efficient exact-and-numerical search.

routes.title: Complex zeros and the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra
routes.description: Count polynomial zeros over the complex numbers, use conjugate pairs for real coefficients, and build real polynomials from complex roots.

routes.title: Building polynomial models and finding numerical roots
routes.description: Construct polynomial functions from conditions, fit vertical scale, and approximate roots that lack convenient exact forms.

routes.title: Rational functions and their domains
routes.description: Identify rational functions and determine all excluded inputs from the original denominator before simplifying.

routes.title: Equivalent formulas, different functions, and holes
routes.description: Identify removable discontinuities caused by common factors and distinguish formula equivalence from function equality.

routes.title: Vertical asymptotes and local behavior
routes.description: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.

routes.title: Horizontal asymptotes and end behavior
routes.description: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.

routes.title: Slant and polynomial asymptotes
routes.description: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.

routes.title: Intercepts and sign charts
routes.description: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.

routes.title: Complete rational graph construction
routes.description: Construct a complete rational graph using domain, discontinuities, asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected values.

routes.title: Rational equations and function intersections
routes.description: Solve rational equations and intersections exactly or numerically while rejecting excluded candidates.

routes.title: Rational inequalities
routes.description: Solve rational inequalities using critical values, sign intervals, and correct endpoint inclusion.

routes.title: Variation and rational models
routes.description: Build and interpret direct, inverse, joint, and combined variation models with meaningful parameters and domains.

routes.title: Partial-fraction structure
routes.description: Decompose proper rational functions with factorable denominators into simpler component fractions and verify recombination.

routes.title: Additive versus multiplicative change
routes.description: Distinguish linear, exponential, and neither patterns by comparing equal-input differences, ratios, and percent changes.

routes.title: Exponential functions and parameters
routes.description: Analyze f(x)=ab^x by interpreting initial value, base, multiplier, percent rate, domain, range, and asymptote.

routes.title: Exponential transformations
routes.description: Analyze transformed exponential functions and track asymptotes, domain, range, and feature points.

routes.title: Growth and decay models
routes.description: Construct exponential models from an initial value, rate, multiplier, two points, or a known doubling or half-life.

routes.title: Compound interest and effective rate
routes.description: Use periodic compounding models and compare nominal rates, periodic rates, compounding frequency, and effective annual yield.

routes.title: Continuous growth and the number e
routes.description: Use A(t)=A0e^(kt) for continuous proportional change and interpret the continuous rate parameter k.

routes.title: Exponential regression and residuals
routes.description: Fit an exponential model to data, interpret parameters, inspect residuals, and evaluate interpolation and extrapolation.

routes.title: Logistic and bounded growth
routes.description: Analyze logistic growth qualitatively and interpret initial value, carrying capacity, growth rate, and inflection behavior.

routes.title: Logarithms as inverse functions
routes.description: Define log base b as the inverse of b^x, convert between forms, and interpret logarithms as exponents.

routes.title: Logarithmic graphs and transformations
routes.description: Analyze transformed logarithmic functions, including domain, range, vertical asymptote, intercepts, and base-dependent direction.

routes.title: Logarithm laws
routes.description: Derive and apply product, quotient, and power laws while preserving positive-argument domains.

routes.title: Solving exponential equations
routes.description: Solve exponential equations using common bases, logarithms, and numerical methods, and interpret exact and approximate answers.

routes.title: Solving logarithmic equations and interpreting inverse models
routes.description: Solve logarithmic equations, reject invalid arguments, and use logarithms to analyze doubling time, half-life, and logarithmic scales.

routes.title: Systems as intersections and models
routes.description: Interpret a system solution as an input-output point satisfying every equation and solve two-variable systems graphically and algebraically.

routes.title: Nonlinear systems
routes.description: Solve systems involving lines, quadratics, circles, rational, exponential, or other nonlinear functions and interpret all real intersections.

routes.title: Systems of inequalities and feasible regions
routes.description: Graph simultaneous inequalities, identify feasible regions, and interpret boundaries and vertices.

routes.title: Systems in three variables
routes.description: Solve and classify three-variable linear systems and interpret their solutions as intersections of planes.

routes.title: Matrix notation and operations
routes.description: Represent rectangular arrays with matrices and perform dimension-compatible addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication.

routes.title: Augmented matrices and row operations
routes.description: Translate linear systems into augmented matrices and justify elementary row operations as equivalent-system transformations.

routes.title: Gaussian elimination and echelon form
routes.description: Use forward elimination to reach row-echelon form and solve by back-substitution.

routes.title: Gauss-Jordan elimination and reduced row-echelon form
routes.description: Reduce matrices to RREF and interpret pivots, free variables, rank, and consistency directly.

routes.title: Determinants, singularity, and inverse matrices
routes.description: Compute and interpret determinants, identify singular matrices, and solve suitable systems with inverse matrices.

routes.title: Linear transformations and multivariable modeling
routes.description: Interpret matrices as transformations of vectors and construct a complete multivariable model using equations, inequalities, and matrices.
